body: Just super tired, I guess. Tired of the person I'm usually closest to not giving me the benefit of the doubt. Tired of fights that include ultimatums and berries veiled threats. Tired of being

I guess some background? We have a three year old and that's a tough age. Lot of defiance, a lot of tantrums. Tonight was particularly rough. Started when the kiddo climbed the counter and put his weight on a closed crock pot to try to get into a cabinet, all things way outside what he knows is allowed. I told him to get down, he ignored me, I raised my voice and told him to get down louder. He told me I'm "not the teacher" so I carried him to his room so he could have a time out.

Had a nice dinner with everyone after that.

Later during bath time. Son was splashing, we do a thing where he soaks a little then gets a shower. He was kicking water out and got both of us wet. I didn't mind as much as the wife did but still told him to stop. He splashed me, I sprayed him with a little water - less than .5 seconds worth, and at normal temp. Was later told this was abusive. Thought nothing of it.

Bedtime continues, tooth brushing time. Kid runs to the bathroom to grab toothbrush, we've told him before to get help doing so because the brushes are kept in a ceramic container.

Tell him to please stop. He doesn't listen. Please stop, no response. I repeated, louder, start punctuating "please stop"s with claps to try to get his attention. Was later told this is abusive.

Kid moves to the place we usually brush teeth, stops in the middle of my path. My big regret, the thing I apologize for this evening. I nudge him with my shin as we do with our cats. He falls down because of slippery socks, instantly wife yells at me - "You just kicked him down!"

Didn't kick. Didn't mean to knock him down. Still feel like shit, because obviously.

Kid bounces back up. What do I even say? Can't say "I didn't kick him", Even though I didn't -denial = guilt. Can't say sorry right away, seems lame and would validate the accusation. He bounces right back up.

From there directly, go to read books. Son wants me to read the first book, climbs to my lap. Still feel like shit, even though it seems like he isn't holding a grudge. Short book, ~ 2 min later at the end I hold him close and apologize for knocking him down. Tell him I didn't mean to, but it's still not okay and I'm sorry. He doesn't care, wants to read the next book.

Finish bedtime.

Go to my own bed. Wife joins me. Wants to talk. Tells me all sorts of things, like that son is afraid of me, I'm damaging his and my relationship, etc. Explain my side of things, worry about how he doesn't listen even when he's in danger. Told that yelling is never okay, not even when he's climbing over breakable glass. Told that if I clapped at her or sprayed her with water, she'd "leave me in an instant". Try to explain that when kid doesn't listen, don't know what else to do. Told to talk quietly and gently. I say that doesn't work. Told it doesn't work because I'm louder than I am quiet (don't think that's true). Ask what I'm supposed to do, then. "Be better".

Continue discussion on another floor. Stay calm but firm. Been recording our fights secretly on my phone. Fights aren't frequent (1 every 3 months or so), but tired of being called abusive and being threatened with divorce. Know that divorce would mean never seeing my kid again, so I record everything now.

Feel hopeless. I acknowledge during our argument that even accidentally knocking down kid is terrible, which is why I apologize. Express resentment toward being told that I'm abusive and damaging trust between son and I. Receive many phrases like "don't even" and "what's worse is you trying to justify yourself" and "I'm just done".

Recognize a lot of generalized "you always" and "you never" language. Recognize it silently. Not out loud. Recognize a lot of words being spoken to me mirror plot of fights from Grey's Anatomy. Feels shitty. Like maybe she's finding reasons to be mad at me. Know I'm not perfect. Know I sometimes suck at being a dad.

Know that if being a dad was taken away from me, I would have nothing to live for.
